# Page 24^page=24
Report Errors in the PDF - support@affairscloud.com Copyright 2014-2026 @ AffairsCloud.com 24 Daily Content PDF NATIONAL AFFAIRS MoEFCC Designates ‘Bhavasagara’ as India’s first National Repository for Deep-Sea Fauna In March 2026, the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC) officially designated the Bhavasagara Referral Centre at Center for Marine Living Resources & Ecology (CMLRE), Kochi, Kerala as India’s first National Repository for Deep-Sea Fauna. • This recognition, granted under section 39 of the Biological Diversity Act, 2002, designates the centre as a key national facility for the conservation, research, and documentation of India’s rich deep-sea biodiversity. Exam Hint: ✓ What? Designated as India’s first National Repository for Deep-Sea Fauna ✓ Name of Centre: Bhavasagara Referral Centre ✓ Designated by: MoEFCC ✓ Parent Organisation: CMLRE, Kochi, Kerala ✓ Purpose: Conservation, research & documentation of deep-sea biodiversity ✓ Legal Provision: Section 39 of the Biological Diversity Act, 2002 About Bhavasagara Referral Centre: Primary Objective: The center’s main goal is to serve as a core platform for ocean scientists to explore and understand the deep sea, while also supporting the growth of India’s blue economy. Purpose: Bhavasagara is a specialized scientific hub and National Repository for preservation, study and documentation of deep-sea marine life. Key Functions: • Maintain Secure Custody: Preserves representative biological samples as voucher specimens along with essential data, including Deoxyribonucleic Acid (DNA) sequences, for future scientific use. • Hold Type Specimens: Serves as the official custodian of newly discovered deep-sea species from Indian waters. • Capacity Building: Promotes expertise in deep-sea taxonomy in line with the United Nations (UN) Decade of Ocean Science for Sustainable Development (2021–2030). Current Holding: The Bhavasagara Referral Centre serves as a key scientific hub, housing over 3,500 taxonomically identified and geo-referenced voucher specimens. • Its collection covers a wide range of marine life, including invertebrates such as cnidarians, annelids, molluscs, arthropods, and echinoderms, as well as vertebrates like elasmobranchs and teleostean fishes. Note: Taxonomy is the science of naming, describing and classifying organisms and includes all plants, animals and microorganisms of the world. About Center for Marine Living Resources & Ecology (CMLRE) The CMLRE is a premier institute under the Ministry of Earth Sciences (MoES), dedicated to the exploration, management, and conservation of marine living resources in the Indian Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ) and adjacent deep seas. Director – Dr M. Sudhakar Established – 1998 About Ministry of Environment, Forest, and Climate Change (MoEFCC): Union Minister– Bhupendra Yadav (Constituency -Alwar, Rajasthan) Minister of State (MoS)– Kirtivardhan Singh (Constituency- Gonda, Uttar Pradesh UP)

# Page 25^page=25
Report Errors in the PDF - support@affairscloud.com Copyright 2014-2026 @ AffairsCloud.com 25 Daily Content PDF India Emerges as Global Leader in Issuing IRCCs under Nagoya Protocol on ABS In March 2026, the National Biodiversity Authority (NBA), Ministry of Environment, Forests, and Climate Change (MoEFCC), announced that India has emerged as the global leader in issuing Internationally Recognised Certificates of Compliance (IRCCs) under the Nagoya Protocol. • As per the data from the Access and Benefit-Sharing (ABS) Clearing-House, India has issued 3,561 IRCCs out of a global total of 6,311, accounting for more than 56% of all certificates issued worldwide. Exam Hints: ✓ What? India Emerges Global Leader in Issuing IRCCs ✓ Informed by: NBA ✓ Framework: Nagoya Protocol on ABS ✓ Total IRCCs Issued: 6,311 (34 countries) ✓ Total IRCCs Issued by India: 3,561 (over 56% of total IRCCs) ✓ Other Leading Countries: France (964), Spain (320), Argentina (257), Panama (156) and Kenya (144). Key Details: Limited Global Participation: So far, only 34 countries out of 142 countries registered on the ABS Clearing-House, issued IRCC. Leading Nations: After India, countries which have issued maximum IRCCs are: France (964), Spain (320), Argentina (257), Panama (156) and Kenya (144). Key Driver for India’s Success: India’s leading position in the fair and equitable use of genetic resources represents the effective implementation of the country’s Access and Benefit-Sharing (ABS) framework under the Biological Diversity Act, 2002. Three-Tier Implementation: This legal framework is currently being implemented via the NBA (at national level); State Biodiversity Boards (SBBs)/ Union Territory (UT) Biodiversity Councils (at state/UT level) and Biodiversity Management Committees (BMCs) (at the local level). About Nagoya Protocol on ABS to CBD: Legal Framework: It is an international legal framework, supplementary to the Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD). It was adopted on October 29, 2010 in Nagoya, Japan but entered into force on October 12, 2014. • In May 2011, India signed the protocol and later ratified it in 2012. Objective: This framework is primarily designed to ensure the effective implementation of one of the three objectives of CBD i.e. ‘the fair and equitable sharing of benefits arising out of the utilization of genetic resources’. IRCC: It is a digital certificate issued by a national authority and published on the ABS Clearing-House to provide legal evidence that a user has accessed genetic resources or traditional knowledge legally. • It ensures the commercial use of genetic resources and traditional knowledge by proving that the user has obtained Prior Informed Consent (PIC) and established Mutually Agreed Terms (MAT) for benefit-sharing with the provider country. About National Biodiversity Authority (NBA): It is a statutory body established under the Biodiversity Act, 2002. It has been mandated to perform, facilitate, regulate and advise the Government of India (GoI) on the issue of conservation, sustainable use of biological resources and fair equitable sharing of benefits of these resources. Chairman- Dr. V.B. Mathur Headquarters- Chennai, Tamil Nadu (TN) Established – 2003

MoE & CBSE Launches AI and Computational Thinking Curriculum for Classes 3–8 In March 2026, the Ministry of Education (MoE) in collaboration with the Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE) launched a new curriculum on Computational Thinking (CT) and Artificial Intelligence (AI) for Classes 3 to 8, to be implemented from the 2026–27 academic session. • The MoE released three key documents, including the curriculum, a teachers’ handbook, and learning materials. Exam Hints ✓ What? Launch of CT & AI curriculum ✓ Who? MoE & CBSE ✓ Classes Covered: 3 to 8 ✓ Focus Areas: AI, coding, data handling, logical reasoning ✓ Aligned With: NEP 2020 & NCF-SE 2023 Key Features of Curriculum: Focus Areas: The curriculum introduces foundational concepts of AI, coding, data handling, logical reasoning, and algorithmic thinking at the elementary and middle school levels. Grade-wise Approach: • Classes 3–5: Activity-based learning with basic computational thinking and logic-building exercises • Classes 6–8: Introduction to AI concepts, coding fundamentals, and real-world applications Alignment: The curriculum aligns with the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020 and the National Curriculum Framework for School Education (NCF-SE) 2023.

Report Errors in the PDF - support@affairscloud.com Copyright 2014-2026 @ AffairsCloud.com 27 Daily Content PDF DoT Extends SIM-Binding Deadline for OTT Platforms to 31 December 2026 In April 2026, the Department of Telecommunications (DoT), under the Ministry of Communications, extended the deadline for Over-The-Top (OTT) platforms to implement Subscriber Identity Module (SIM)- binding by 31st December 2026. • The move revised the earlier 90-day compliance timeline issued on 28 November 2025, which came into effect from 1 March 2026. Exam Hints: ✓ What? SIM-binding deadline extended for OTT Platforms ✓ By whom? DoT, Ministry of Communication ✓ New Deadline: 31 December 2026 ✓ Rule: Telecommunications (Telecom Cyber Security) Rules, 2024 ✓ Key Change: Removal of 6-hour automatic logout rule ✓ Purpose: Prevent cyber frauds. About SIM-Binding Policy Update: Approach: The DoT replaced the earlier six-hour automatic logout rule with a risk-based mechanism where sessions are terminated only in suspected fraud cases, addressing concerns over user inconvenience. Framework: The directive was issued under the Telecommunications (Telecom Cyber Security) Rules, 2024, within the Telecommunications Act, 2023 framework that replaced the Indian Telegraph Act, 1885. SIM-Binding: SIM-binding requires OTT applications to remain continuously linked to a mobile number, preventing use without an active SIM and aiming to curb cybercrimes like digital arrest scams and financial frauds while enhancing user verification. BCGCL and MCL Sign Land Lease Agreement for India’s First Indigenous Coal-to-Ammonium Nitrate Project On April 1 2026, Bharat Coal Gasification and Chemicals Limited (BCGCL) and Mahanadi Coalfields Limited (MCL), a subsidiary of Coal India Limited (CIL), signed a landmark land lease agreement for setting up India’s first indigenous coal-to-ammonium nitrate project at Lakhanpur, Odisha. • The MoU was signed in the presence of Union Minister G. Kishan Reddy, Ministry of Coal and Ministry of Mines (MoM) and Vikram Dev Dutt, Secretary, Ministry of Coal, in New Delhi (Delhi). Exam Hints: ✓ What? Land Lease Agreement signed ✓ Entities: BCGCL & MCL ✓ Purpose: To set up India’s first indigenous coal-to-ammonium nitrate project at Lakhanpur, Odisha ✓ Capacity: 2,000 tonnes per day (TPD) ✓ Investment: Rs 25,000 crore ✓ Technology: Coal gasification (BHEL) About Coal-to-Ammonium Nitrate Project: Agreement: The project, designed as a 2,000 tonnes per day (TPD) ammonium nitrate facility, marks a significant milestone for India’s energy and chemical sectors. Technology: The project will use indigenously developed gasification technology by Bharat Heavy Electricals Limited (BHEL). Investment: The project involves an estimated investment of Rs 25,000 crore with financial support of Rs 1,350 crore from the Ministry of Coal.

INTERNATIONAL AFFAIRS CMS COP15 Concluded Successfully in Brazil with 40 new Species Being Accorded Protection The 15th Meeting of the Conference of the Parties (COP15) to the Convention on the Conservation of Migratory Species of Wild Animals (CMS) was held under Brazil Presidency from 23 to 29 March 2026 in Campo Grande, Brazil. • During the conference, a total of 40 species, subspecies, and populations were newly included or reclassified under Appendices I and II, of which 16 are found in Brazil. Exam Hints: ✓ What? CMS COP15 (15th Conference of Parties) held ✓ Where? Campo Grande, Brazil (COP Presidency) ✓ Theme: “Connecting Nature to Sustain Life” ✓ Key Outcome: 40 species added/reclassified under Appendix I & II ✓ Report Highlight (2026): 49% species declining; 24% at risk of extinction; 188 species facing extinction ✓ COP16: Germany in 2029. About CMS COP15: Overview: CMS COP15, a major global wildlife conservation meeting, brought together representatives from 132 countries and the European Union (EU) under the theme “Connecting Nature to Sustain Life.” Global Concern on Migratory Species: According to the ‘State of the World’s Migratory Species Report 2026’, nearly 49% of migratory species populations are declining, around 24% face the risk of extinction. • According to the report, a total of 188 migratory species are currently facing the risk of extinction, including 28 terrestrial mammals, 23 aquatic mammals, 103 bird species, 8 reptile species, and 26 fish species. • The major threats include overexploitation such as hunting and fishing, habitat loss, and the fragmentation of migratory routes. • The analysis found that 47% of the 9,000 Key Biodiversity Areas (KBAs) identified as vital for migratory species lack any formal protection or conservation measures. Key Outcomes of COP15: A total of 40 migratory species, including birds, aquatic and terrestrial animals, were brought under CMS protection. • Notable species added to the list include the striped hyena (Hyaena hyaena), cheetah (Acinonyx jubatus), giant otter (Pteronura brasiliensis), great hammerhead shark (Sphyrna mokarran), snowy owl (Bubo scandiacus), and Hudsonian godwit (Limosa haemastica). Future Developments: Brazil assumed the presidency for the next three years to oversee the implementation of decisions, while Germany was announced as the host of COP16 in 2029 to mark the 50th anniversary of CMS. • India hosted CMS COP13 in Gandhinagar, Gujarat in 2020, where the Great Indian Bustard, Asian Elephant, and Bengal Florican were added to Appendix I. About Bonn Convention: Bonn Convention: The Convention on the Conservation of Migratory Species of Wild Animals (CMS), also known as the Bonn Convention, is a legally binding international treaty under the United Nations

Objective: CMS promotes international cooperation to conserve migratory species, their habitats, and migration routes across countries (Range States). Classification of Species: • Appendix I: Includes migratory species in danger of extinction. Member states are legally obliged to strictly protect these animals and prohibit their taking/killing. • Appendix II: Includes species that would significantly benefit from international cooperation and coordinated management across their migratory range. Member Obligations: CMS member countries are legally required to protect endangered migratory species, conserve and restore habitats, remove migration barriers, and cooperate with other range states. About United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP): Executive Director (ED)– Inger Andersen (Denmark) Headquarters– Nairobi, Kenya Established– 1972 Members – 193 Member States BANKING & FINANCE IRDAI Approves India AS Framework For Insurers From April 1, 2026 In March 2026, the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI) approved the IRDAI (Actuarial, Finance and Investment Functions of Insurers) (Amendment) Regulations, 2026 at its 135th Authority Meeting. Exam Hints ✓ What? IRDAI approves IRDAI (Actuarial, Finance and Investment Functions of Insurers) (Amendment) Regulations, 2026 ✓ Purpose: Mandates preparation of financial statements with Ind AS ✓ Effective from: 1st April 2026 ✓ Applicable to: Life, General Stand Along Health Insurers and Reinsurers. ✓ Parallel Reporting: Reporting in old and new standard for 2 years ✓ Expert group: Expert group headed by Mr. Rajay Kumar Sinha WTM (Finance and Investment) for 2 years Key Highlights Implementation: The amendments mandate the preparation and presentation of financial statements by insurers in accordance with applicable Indian Accounting Standards (Ind AS), with effect from 1st April 2026. Applicable to: The implementation will be applicable to all categories of insurers including Life, General Stand Along Health Insurers and Reinsurers. Expert Group Joint Export: The IRDAI constituted a joint expert group on IndAS, chaired by the Whole Time Member (WTM) (Finance and Investment), IRDAI currently Mr. Rajay Kumar Sinha. • The group shall remain in force for a period of 2 years from the date of constitution.

Function: As the deputy professional head, the officer serves as a senior adviser to the Ministry of Defence (MoD) and manages strategic planning and operational logistics. ACQUISITIONS & MERGERS RBI Approves Emirates NBD’s 60% Stake Acquisition in RBL Bank In April 2026, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) approved Emirates NBD’s acquisition of a 60% stake in RBL Bank, through a preferential allotment of equity shares, in a deal valued at around Rs 26,853 crore. • The approval also covers the merger of existing operations of Emirates NBD in India with RBL, subject to requisite regulatory clearances. Exam Hints: ✓ What? RBI approved acquisition of stake in RBL Bank ✓ Acquirer: Emirates NBD ✓ Stake: 60% ✓ Deal Value: Rs 26,853 crore ✓ Mode: Preferential allotment, open offer. Key Details of Acquisition: Acquisition Process: Emirates NBD will launch an open offer to buy a maximum 26% of RBL’s voting share capital at a price of Rs 280 per equity share. • In addition, the mandatory offer, related to the planned acquisition will include around 415.58 million shares. Key Change in Role: Upon completion of the transaction, Emirates NBD will be designated as a promoter of RBL Bank, which will become its largest subsidiary outside India. Regulatory Status: While the RBI’s approval has advanced the process, the deal is now pending clearance from the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI). About RBL Bank: It formerly known as Ratnakar Bank Limited, is a private sector bank in India, established in 1943 and headquartered in Mumbai, Maharashtra.
